title: tk herd reconcile: crash recovery from durable state
description: cmd/tk/cmd/herd_reconcile.go + internal/herd/reconcile. tk herd reconcile [--epic <id>] [--json]: rebuild run state after orchestrator death per herdr-runner.md reconcile order — tracker in_progress ticks + runner-state notes, manifests under .tick/logs/herd/, git worktree list + branch --list with the configured worktree_branch_prefix, live herdr agent list, api snapshot agent_session ids. Classify each in-flight tick: live-worker (continue via prompt), dead-worker-resumable (emit the exact per-kind resume command from herdr-kinds.md translation), dead-with-work (redispatch from branch), stale-no-work (safe reset), unknown (surface, never auto-reset). Output a structured plan; mutate NOTHING (the orchestrator acts on the plan) except optionally --adopt to refresh manifests for live workers found consistent. Never propose a second branch for a tick with recoverable work. Cobra + legacy switch + ResetFlags. Unit tests: fake server + fixture manifests/repos for each classification incl. the live-worker-must-not-redispatch case.
notes: 2026-08-11 15:10 - Dispatch requirement (human-approved): every herd command must return explicit ExitError for its exit codes — never rely on GetExitCode message-substring classification (known to misread "invalid argument" dial errors as usage exit 2). Pattern established in herd_wait.go (tick 9z6).
acceptance_criteria: go test -short -count=1 ./... passes; all five classifications covered by tests; reconcile is read-only apart from --adopt manifest refresh
